purpose: 依 SC-049 事前凍結的 1M/2M/3M 候選落後期，加入第三個台灣鋼鐵鏈版本並建立第二條非鋼鐵三層月度候選鏈，檢查是否存在可重播且不靠事後挑 lag 的供應鏈 Lead-Lag。

july.pitRule: July monthly averages were published after July; they are not usable for a July decision state.

augustSeptember.sourceClockRule: Use capturedAt conservatively for prospective replay unless native publication timestamp is separately frozen.

frozenLagReplay.reasonInsufficient: Two pairs are too few for a stable lag claim and can be generated by common demand, inventory or repricing cycles.

downstreamPassThrough.implication: A possible scrap-to-billet lag does not imply the same lag continues to H-beam.

commonShockAndAlternativeExplanations: The August report states replenishment support faded and Q3 traditional low season weakened terminal procurement.
Manufacturers were consuming inventory and controlling purchasing cadence.
EU quota/trade restrictions and weak export conditions affected downstream demand and market competition.
Raw-material price decline and major-mill price cuts can move several chain layers together.
Billet can respond to independent billet demand, electricity, freight, yield and inventory rather than only scrap.
H-beam price stickiness can reflect posted-price/contract reset cadence rather than absence of cost pressure.
Monthly averages hide within-month ordering and repricing timing.

result.keyCounterexample: Orders rose in all three months while middle/downstream monthly production directions flipped.
result.commonShock: MOEA narratives for all three months directly cite AI/HPC/cloud-related demand as a major driver of multiple layers.
result.overseasProductionFirewall: Export orders are not equivalent to Taiwan domestic production; overseas production is material. MOEA survey evidence reports electronic-product orders have a substantial but not 100% domestic-production share.
result.taxonomyFirewall: Product-order categories and production-industry classifications are not a one-to-one physical supplier graph.

negativeControls.role: weak nonlinked/control lane showing broad manufacturing strength did not lift all industries

negativeControls.control: August motor vehicles and parts production
negativeControls.role: weak nonlinked/control lane; not exposure-matched enough for causal estimation

positiveEvidence: The steel chain now has three sequential monthly vintages.
The 1M lag candidate was frozen before the third-vintage interpretation and produces 2/2 directional scrap-to-billet matches.
A second non-steel monthly three-layer candidate with official release clocks was constructed.
counterevidence: The prefrozen 2M steel lag already has a contradiction.
H-beam stayed flat across all three steel months.
The electronics candidate does not show stable three-layer directional propagation.
Common AI demand is explicitly identified by MOEA as a simultaneous driver across electronics layers.
Electronic export orders include overseas production and do not prove a Taiwan physical supplier graph.
Steel native first-known publication clocks are not uniformly frozen across all three monthly vintages.

reasonNoD10_02L3: SC-049's local promotion gate is not yet satisfied. The apparent 1M scrap-to-billet relation has only two matured pairs, the 2M candidate already contradicts, downstream H-beam does not propagate, the second electronics chain falsifies a universal fixed-lag story, and fully compatible first-known clocks/physical graph semantics remain incomplete.

systemImplications.system1: Do not add a fixed supply-chain lag score or positive bonus. Current evidence supports only research context and future preregistered testing.
systemImplications.system2: A future context lane may preserve chain-specific lag hypotheses and confidence/UNKNOWN states, but no timing action or vote is authorized.

exactNext: SC-054 append at least three additional independent steel vintages so 1M/2M/3M candidates have enough matured pairs without changing the frozen lag set.
Build one second non-steel physical issuer/product chain with effective-dated supplier/customer or product-flow evidence rather than only aggregate demand categories.
Freeze comparable first-known/source publication clocks for every monthly node before any L3 promotion.
Test lag stability after inventory, contract repricing, seasonality and common-demand controls; preserve contradictions instead of selecting the best-looking lag.
